IR.rationale: REITs behave like long-duration bond proxies. A rise in intermediate yields together with bear steepening raises discount rates and cap-rate pressure, which weighs on subsequent REIT returns.

B.rationale: A credit sell-off (Baa spreads widening, high-yield falling) signals a temporary rise in risk premia. Levered real estate tends to recover from such episodes as the premia are partly unwound.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility proxies a high price of risk. It is associated with higher subsequent expected returns on risky, levered assets such as REITs.

AP.rationale: Strong recent market excess returns tend to partially reverse at weekly-to-monthly horizons. REITs, with their high market beta, share in that reversal.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of conservative-investment firms marks a defensive, yield-oriented style rotation. Such rotations favour asset-heavy, low-growth sectors like REITs.

FX.rationale: A strengthening broad dollar reflects tightening global dollar liquidity and risk appetite. That matters for funding-sensitive real-estate valuations.

COM.rationale: Silver rallies often accompany reflation and inflation scares. Those push real yields and rate expectations in a direction that hurts rate-sensitive REITs.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens in loose financial conditions point to reflation and tighter policy ahead. That raises discount rates for income-oriented real estate.

ENDG.rationale: Short-horizon REIT returns show mild reversal, consistent with liquidity-driven overshooting in a rate-sensitive sector.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates signal flight to quality and growth scares. These episodes precede turbulent trading in rate- and credit-sensitive real estate.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit (falling high-yield prices, widening Baa spreads) tightens funding for levered property owners. It foreshadows higher equity volatility through the leverage and funding channels.

V.rationale: Elevated cross-asset implied volatility beyond equities, here gold, signals macro and safe-haven uncertainty. Recent REIT realised variance may not yet reflect it.

AP.rationale: Joint weakness in US and EM equities is a global risk-off state. Through the leverage effect and volatility feedback, such states raise future variance.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms indicates flight to quality within equities, typical of stressed markets that precede higher volatility.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength combined with yen appreciation is the classic safe-haven, carry-unwind configuration associated with rising risk-asset volatility.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity declines signal weakening global demand and deflationary shocks. Both tend to come with elevated financial-market volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise funding costs and reduce liquidity provision. That amplifies price swings in levered, financing-dependent sectors such as REITs.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is persistent but mean-reverting. When recent variance is high against its history, part of it decays faster than a simple persistence model implies.

IR.rationale: A sharp bear steepening with rising intermediate yields is the rate shock most damaging to bond-proxy REITs, raising the odds of a tail loss.

B.rationale: Credit stress raises refinancing risk for levered real estate. It increases the probability of a disorderly REIT sell-off.

V.rationale: Simultaneously elevated equity and safe-haven implied volatility marks a high-uncertainty regime in which the return distribution widens and left-tail events become more likely.

AP.rationale: Small-cap underperformance signals deteriorating liquidity and risk appetite. That is a headwind for the mid-cap, financing-dependent REIT universe.

ST.rationale: Quality outperformance reflects defensive repositioning that tends to precede stressed equity episodes.

FX.rationale: A falling Australian dollar is a barometer of global risk aversion and carry unwinds, which raises downside tail risk in risky assets.

COM.rationale: Precious-metal rallies reflect either hedging demand or inflation scares. Both are associated with heightened downside risk for rate-sensitive REITs.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with elevated measured stress identify funding-constrained regimes in which large drawdowns in levered sectors cluster.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns go with volatility clustering and forced deleveraging, so further large losses are more likely in the short run.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate lower discount rates. They can trigger sharp rallies in bond-like real-estate equities.

B.rationale: After spread widening, risk premia are elevated. Their subsequent compression can produce outsized rebounds in levered REITs.

V.rationale: High implied volatility and policy uncertainty widen the return distribution and raise risk premia. That makes large relief rallies more likely as well as large losses.

AP.rationale: Value outperformance marks rotations toward cheap, asset-heavy sectors. REITs typically load positively on value.

ST.rationale: Conservative-investment outperformance signals demand for defensive, high-payout stocks, which can lift REITs sharply.

FX.rationale: Yen strength marks risk-off episodes accompanied by falling yields. Bond-proxy REITs can benefit strongly from such moves, and rebound after them.

COM.rationale: Commodity weakness lowers inflation expectations and rate pressure. That supports sharp rallies in income-oriented real estate.

MC.rationale: Stressed, tight conditions widen the return distribution. Easing of that stress, often aided by policy response, tends to produce large rebounds.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns raise the chance of a sharp short-horizon reversal, as liquidity-driven selling overshoots.
